reviewedFrom: B07.1 definition of done (advisor-plans/013) and the dimension matrix in docs/books-dimensions.md; tag policy decided 2026-10-06: reporting tags stay as posted. B07.2 definition of done.

matrix-on-lines.derivation: One job in the South division, on lot 14 of Cedar Ridge, with one fixed-price contract. A 1,000.00 framing bill coded to its cost code, a 1,000.00 progress invoice and its full payment post. Every line on a project carries the project's tags (organization, division, community, lot, contract; names beside ids). The bill's cost line adds cost_type and cost_code_id; its AP line carries the project tags only. The invoice (percentage of completion under the fixed contract) carries the project tags on both lines. The payment carries the project tags plus the payment and the invoice it settles on both lines.

foreign-dimension-refused.derivation: An adjusting journal tagging another company's cost code on the job is refused because the cost code is not in this company; so is one naming a cost code that does not exist. The same journal naming the company's own cost code posts.

one-lot-per-project.derivation: A project's lot tag is never a guess because a project sits on at most one lot: putting the job on a second lot is refused by the database (lots_project_unique). Several contracts on one project leave contract_id off its lines until contract-level ownership (B04.1) assigns each document a contract.

later-changes-and-reversal.derivation: A bill posts in the South division. The community is renamed and the job moves to the North division; the ordinary run and the nightly pass leave the posted lines exactly as they were. Re-coding the bill to materials is a real revision: the original entry is reversed with its original dimensions line for line (South division), and the replacement posts in the North division.

statements-by-tag.derivation: July: framing of 1,000.00 on the South-division job (fixed contract, so its 1,000.00 invoice is a contract liability, not revenue), framing of 500.00 on a North-division job, office rent of 200.00 and office payroll of 500.00 (two workers, 300.00 and 200.00) with no job. Net income is -2,200.00 and every slicing (division, community, lot, contract, cost code, cost type, organization, project) totals exactly -2,200.00. By division: South -1,000.00, North -500.00, and the untagged office costs visible as Unassigned -700.00. The South framing slice drills to its one 1,000.00 line. The customer payment on the undeposited-funds register opens the invoice it settled. A bookkeeper limited to assigned divisions is refused the statements and the general ledger. The owner sees the two payroll lines (200.00 and 300.00); a Books reviewer without private payroll access sees one merged 500.00 line.

closed-month-as-closed.derivation: A 1,000.00 bill posts on a fixed-price job in July, the month's WIP review recognizes 1,250.00 of revenue and July closes. A copy of the bill's journal is then written into closed July straight to the database, around every guard. The July P&L is served as it was closed: its heading says 'as closed' with the close date, it shows net income of 250.00, and its CSV carries the same line, while a live rebuild of July reads -750.00.

fiscal-comparisons.derivation: A company whose fiscal year starts in April records overhead of 10.00 (May 2025), 20.00 (March 2026), 40.00 (April 2026) and 80.00 (February 2027). Fiscal 2026 (April 2026 to March 2027) shows 120.00; its prior-year comparison is exactly fiscal 2025 (April 2025 to March 2026), 30.00; March to April 2026, across the fiscal year-end, shows 60.00.
